open_points.subject: temporary store cleanup in write-ahead-log mode
open_points.text: “a store made new is made in SQLite's write-ahead-log mode” but at the next start Registry “removes a file of that temporary name ... and no other file there”
open_points.question: When an interrupted creation of the temporary SQLite store leaves WAL companion files such as the temporary store's `-wal` or `-shm` file, must the next start remove those companions, leave them, or fail?
options: Treat the WAL companion files as parts of the temporary store and remove them with its main file.
Remove only the main temporary file as the text literally requires, leaving its WAL companion files.
Fail the start if any WAL companion file of the temporary store exists.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the specifically named SQLite WAL companion files as parts of the temporary store and remove them before recreating it.

witness.initial: The configured store is absent and no earlier temporary store exists.
events: Registry starts, creates the declared temporary SQLite store, puts it in write-ahead-log mode and writes the new store's schema/version.
The process is interrupted before the temporary store is renamed or SQLite performs clean shutdown, leaving the temporary main file and one or both WAL companion files.
Registry starts again and applies the rule that removes the file of the temporary name “and no other file there”.
outcomes: An implementer removes only the temporary main file and leaves the WAL companion files; recreating or opening the same temporary name may encounter or recover those stale companions, or the files remain indefinitely.
An implementer treats the companion files as part of the temporary store and removes them too before recreation, despite the instruction to remove no other file.
witness.observer: The owner sees different leftover files, and the next start can differ in whether it succeeds or what temporary database SQLite opens.

open_points.subject: backup snapshot instant
open_points.text: “the instant being that of the read that fixes its snapshot” and “the instant is read from the clock at that read”
open_points.question: Must the clock be sampled before or after the SQLite read that fixes the snapshot, and what ordering must the recorded instant have relative to a commit racing that read?
options: Sample the clock immediately before the database read that fixes the snapshot.
Fix the database snapshot first, then sample the clock.
Define one explicit linearization point and require both the snapshot and recorded instant to be attributed to it.
open_points.default_guess: Define the database read that fixes the snapshot as the linearization point and sample the clock immediately before issuing that read.

witness.initial: The store is in write-ahead-log mode with audit counter 10, and a writer is ready to commit change 11 while a backup begins.
events: The backup establishes its snapshot by its first read of the audit counter.
The writer commits change 11 during the interval in which the implementation performs that database read and samples the wall clock.
The kept backup exposes its recorded instant; after restore, the owner can inspect whether change 11 is present.
outcomes: An implementation that samples the clock before issuing the read can record an instant before change 11's commit while its subsequently fixed snapshot includes change 11.
An implementation that fixes the snapshot before sampling the clock can record an instant after change 11's commit while its snapshot excludes change 11.
witness.observer: The owner sees a backup timestamp whose ordering relative to change 11 disagrees with whether the restored backup contains that change.
